gbr_the_ladies_waldegrave.webp

A faithful oil painting reproduction of Joshua Reynolds' 'The Ladies Waldegrave' (1780), exact composition of the original, not mirrored, not reimagined. Three young sisters in white muslin dresses sit side by side at a small polished mahogany table covered with a deep red cloth, in a softly lit Georgian interior. All three wear tall powdered grey-white hair piled high in the 1780s fashion. Left: Lady Charlotte holds a skein of white silk thread between her hands. Centre: Lady Elizabeth winds the silk from it. Right: Lady Anna bends over a white tambour embroidery frame, tambouring with a needle. Their faces are pale and rosy with downcast eyes. Behind them: a dark olive-brown wall and a heavy deep crimson curtain at upper left, with a glimpse of a dim landscape through a window. Warm, feathery, Grand Manner brushwork, creamy whites against dark umber, red accents. Square 1:1. A faithful reproduction of Guercino's Baroque oil painting 'Et in Arcadia Ego' (c. 1618-22, Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica, Rome), exact composition of the original, not mirrored, not reimagined. Two young shepherds stand at the left, half in shadow, one leaning on a staff, both gazing down in surprise at a large weathered human skull lying on a low crumbling stone wall in the lower right foreground. Beside the skull, a small fly and a field mouse; carved on the stone below are the words ET IN ARCADIA EGO. A dark tree trunk and foliage frame the left, and behind the shepherds a dusky landscape with warm amber-grey evening sky and distant hills. Rich chiaroscuro, earthy umber, olive, russet and ochre, loose Baroque brushwork. Square 1:1. Right: Saint Barbara in olive and gold robes kneels with eyes lowered. The background is a glowing golden-white sky filled with faint cloud-like cherub faces. Green curtains are pulled open at both upper corners. At the bottom, two small winged cherubs lean on the ledge, resting their chins on their arms, looking up. A faithful reproduction of Théodore Géricault's Romantic oil painting 'The Raft of the Medusa' (1818-19, Louvre), exact composition of the original, not mirrored, not reimagined. A faithful photographic reproduction of the ancient marble sculpture group 'Laocoön and His Sons' (Vatican Museums), exact composition of the original, not mirrored, not reimagined. White-grey weathered marble: the bearded priest Laocoön sits in the centre on an altar, his powerful body twisting, his right arm raised high above his head, his face anguished, a cloth draped over his lap; a large sea serpent coils around him. A young son stands on the left and a second son on the right, both entwined by the serpent's coils. Soft museum light from the left, cool shadows, realistic marble texture. The sculpture is centred and fills the square 1:1 frame, against a plain neutral dark grey background only, with no pedestal, walls, room, columns or other objects.
